title: Driftward Plateau
description: An asymmetric faulted limestone island with a long keel, detached fragments and a grass-capped summit. The keel starts near Z=0.

review.notes: New budget round 3 (last): rejected, escalate. Fixed: the soffit undersides are now grey limestone matching the faces, with no cream tint, stretch or black zigzag lines; the faces show larger bed planes between the joints in the turn tiles; the keel tip is fractured and textured; the meadow rocks are rounded, half-buried split boulders; the satellites have turf caps; a brown soil band now shows under the turf lip. Still failing: (1) form_detail 7: the new remesh has melted the rock. In the closeup the cliff faces are soft, rounded, pale columns like wax or soap with no crisp fracture edges, the soffits hang in drooping, dripping lobes (closeup_base upper half), and the keel tip is lumpy crumpled noise rather than broken planes (closeup_base lower centre). (2) material 7: in the closeup the faces render near pure white with smeared, low-contrast texture and no joint darkening or weathering, unlike the grey jointed limestone in the turn tiles. (3) defects 7: the soil band is a thin, even brown ribbon with a clean edge along the whole rim; the roots do not read and the turf sits on it like a flat sheet; hanging grass shows only at one spot. Fix: lower the remesh smoothing or re-sharpen after it so the fracture planes and joint edges stay crisp; break the soffit lobes into angular spalls; use the turn-tile limestone shading in the close range too (darker joints, rain streaks); vary the soil band 0.3-0.8 m with bulges, exposed root clusters and grass hanging over the lip.
